## Find the correlation with US Karen data and the other three countries in the future 50 years. (assume only female Karens)

```{r}
library(dplyr)
data <- full_names_data_nice
```

```{r}
helperCorLagKaren <- function(name_data, lagN, karen_data) {
  tryCatch(cor(name_data$prop, lag(karen_data$prop, lagN), method = "kendall", use = "complete.obs"), error = function(i) {
    return(NA)
  })
}
```

```{r}
data_united_states <- data %>% filter(country == "United States", name == "Karen", sex == "Girl")
```

```{r}
data_england_wales <- data %>% filter(country == "England/Wales", name == "Karen", sex == "Girl")
```

```{r}
data_scotland <- data %>% filter(country == "Scotland", name == "Karen", sex == "Girl")
```

```{r}
data_northern_irerland <- data %>% filter(country == "Nothern Ireland", name == "Karen", sex == "Girl")
```

```{r}
helperCorLagKaren(data_united_states, 50, data_england_wales)
```
```{r}
helperCorLagKaren(data_united_states, 50, data_scotland)
```

```{r}
helperCorLagKaren(data_united_states, 50, data_northern_irerland)
```
